**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on Surah 66, verses 6–8:**

﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾. Khaythama said: "Everything in the Qur'an that begins with 'O you who have believed' is, in the Torah, 'O you poor ones (al-masakin)'."

Ibn Mas'ud said: "When God says 'O you who have believed,' give it your attentive hearing, for it is either something good you are commanded to do or something evil you are forbidden from."

al-Zuhri said: "When God, exalted is He, says 'O you who have believed, do,' the Prophet is among them."

The meaning of His words ﴿protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ is: turn the Fire away from them. From this is the verse of the rajaz poet:

"Had one been able to ward off death, the protector would have warded it off; but how can one ward off what death has already reached?"

(p-44)

On this verse there are three interpretations:

First: its meaning is "Protect yourselves, and let your families protect themselves from the Fire." This is related from al-Dahhak.

Second: "Protect yourselves, and command your families to remember God and to supplicate, until God protects you through them." This is narrated by Ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas.

Third: "Protect yourselves by your deeds, and protect your families by your instruction." This is said by Ali, Qatada and Mujahid.

Regarding the instruction that protects them from the Fire, there are three sayings. First: he commands them to obey God and forbids them from disobeying Him; this is said by Qatada. Second: he teaches them their obligations and disciplines them in their worldly life; this is said by Ali. Third: he teaches them good, commands them to do it, makes evil clear to them, and forbids them from it.

Muqatil said: "That obligation is upon him regarding himself, his offspring, his slaves and his female slaves."

﴿Its fuel is people and stones﴾. Regarding the mention of stones along with people there are three sayings. First: they are the stones that they worshipped, so that they witness what brought about their destination to the Fire; God has made this clear in His words ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell﴾. Second: they are stones of sulphur, which increase the Fire's fuel, and their mention was an addition to the threat and the punishment; this is said by Ibn Mas'ud and Mujahid. Third: He mentioned the stones so that they would know that whatever burns stones burns people even more intensely.

Ibn Abi Za'ida narrated, saying: "It reached me that the Messenger of God ﷺ recited this verse, ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves﴾ up to the end of the verse, while some of his companions were with him, including an elderly man. The old man said: 'O Messenger of God, are the stones of Hell like the stones of this world?' He said: 'By Him in whose hand my soul is, a single rock of Hell is greater than all the mountains of this world.' The old man fainted, so the Prophet ﷺ placed his hand on his heart, and he was alive. He said: 'O old man, say: there is no god but God.' He said it, and he gave him the good news of Paradise. His companions said: 'O Messenger of God, is he among us?' He said: 'Yes, by the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿That is for one who fears My standing and fears My threat﴾.'"

(p-45)

﴿Over it are angels, stern and severe﴾: meaning, hard of hearts and severe in their actions; they are the Zabaniyah (the angels of punishment).

﴿They do not disobey God in what He commands them﴾: that is, they do not oppose His command by adding to it or subtracting from it.

﴿And they do what they are commanded﴾: that is, at its appointed time, so they neither delay it nor advance it.

﴿O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance (tawbatan nasuha)﴾. On this there are five interpretations. First: sincere repentance (al-tawba al-nasuh) is the truthful and sincere repentance; this is said by Qatada. Second: "sincere" means that one hates the sin one once loved and seeks forgiveness for it whenever one remembers it; this is said by al-Hasan. Third: that one does not trust in its acceptance and remains in fear of it. Fourth: that it is the repentance after which one needs no further repentance. Fifth: that one repents from the sin and never returns to it; this is said by Umar ibn al-Khattab.

According to these interpretations, the word (nasuh) is derived from al-nisaha, which is sewing.

Regarding its derivation from sewing, there are two views. First: because it is a repentance that has firmly secured obedience to Him and tightened it, just as a tailor secures a garment by stitching and fastening it. Second: because it has joined the penitent with the friends of God and attached him to them, just as a tailor gathers the cloth and joins one part to another.

Nu'aym narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed God, exalted is He, is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than one of you is at his lost camel which he finds in a barren desert, upon which are his provisions and his water."

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 66, verses 9–10:

﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them.﴾ As for striving against the disbelievers, it is with the sword. As for striving against the hypocrites, there are four aspects to it:

The first: it is with the tongue and speech. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak.

The second: it is with sternness toward them, as Allah mentioned. This was said by al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas.

The third: with one's hand; if one is not able, then with one's tongue; if one is not able, then with one's heart, and let him face them with a scowling countenance. This was said by Ibn Masʿud.

The fourth: by enforcing the hudud (prescribed punishments) upon them. This was said by al-Hasan.

﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them.﴾ Regarding their betrayal, there are four aspects:

The first: they were both disbelievers, so they became betrayers through disbelief. This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: they were two hypocrites who showed faith and concealed disbelief, and this was their betrayal. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The wife of a prophet never committed adultery at all; their betrayal was only in the religion."

The third: their betrayal was tale-bearing; when Allah the Exalted revealed [something] to them, they would divulge it to the polytheists. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The fourth: the betrayal of Noah's wife was that she would tell people that he was mad, and whenever anyone believed in him, she would inform the tyrants about him. And the betrayal of Lot's wife was that whenever a guest came to him, she would light smoke to inform her people that a guest had arrived, because of what they were upon of going after men.

Muqatil said: The name of Noah's wife was Walihah, and the name of Lot's wife was Wali'ah.

Al-Dahhak said, from ʿAʾishah, that Gabriel descended upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him that the name of Noah's wife was Wa'ilah, and the name of Lot's wife was Waliha.

﴿But they availed them nothing against Allah at all.﴾ That is, Noah and Lot, despite their honor with Allah, did not avert from their wives, when they disobeyed, anything of Allah's punishment, as an alert that punishment is averted by obedience, not by mere kinship as a means.

Yahya ibn Salam said: This is an example that Allah set forth to warn Hafsah and ʿAʾishah when they colluded against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then He set forth for them an example with the wife of Pharaoh and Maryam, daughter of ʿImran, encouraging adherence to obedience, saying:

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 66, verses 11–12:
